title: Energy-Aware HPC Scheduling with LLM-Based Power Prediction
problem: HPC energy consumption strains grid; need operational strategies to manage HPC as grid load
motivation: Theoretical energy-aware scheduling studied; lack practical implementations; grid integration critical
method: The approach trains a large language model (LLM) to predict how much power each computing job will consume by analyzing its characteristics. Based on these predictions, a lightweight scheduling strategy shifts when jobs run to align with grid conditions or renewable energy availability. The system integrates into Slurm, the job scheduler widely used in data centers, without modifying its core code, making deployment straightforward.
key_novelty: Using learned representations from a language model (LLM embeddings), the approach predicts job power with 15% lower error than prior methods, enabling a 4.0 MWh shift of computing load to solar-peak hours without reducing throughput.
contributions: LLM-based power prediction from job scripts
Energy-aware scheduling without Slurm core modification
Per-job power MAE reduction (15% vs SOTA)
